answer.rationale: Primary contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line sits at 94% with zero buffer, so a primary cutover would raise delivery risk and violate the objective even though the low-cost quote alone hits the 18% spend cut. Inherited renewal experience is that market benchmarking moved the incumbent on price and terms (c4) and that staying put avoided migration and missed deliveries (c1); multi-year volume structure (c6) can be part of that ask. Prior low-cost primary switch (c2) is the main competing lesson but is unverified and may not transfer into a two-week, no-buffer window—hence verify c4 and c2. Second-source and defer leave the expiring primary unsolved. Uncertain whether the incumbent will actually concede the full 18%.
